title: bug: JetBrains readDaemonInfo deletes same-project Windows/WSL daemon.json spellings before the live identity probe
description:
In MoeDaemonSupervisor.readDaemonInfo (lines 58–63), File(info.projectPath).canonicalPath is compared to File(base).canonicalPath and mismatch deletes daemon.json. Repro on Windows: base D:/proj, daemon.json projectPath /mnt/d/proj; these canonical paths differ although they identify the same cross-OS project, so connect never reaches DaemonIdentityProbe.
The same reader can delete a newly rewritten metadata file during handleForeignDaemon's re-read before its pid/port/startedAt guard. Found in task-90664db1 review; MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt is explicitly outside that task's scope. Add bounded/read-only identity parsing and cross-OS path regression coverage without changing RF activation rules.
definitionOfDone: Windows drive, slash, and /mnt/<drive> spellings of the same project do not delete live daemon metadata before health probing.
The foreign-daemon compare-delete path cannot remove a rewritten file through side effects of readDaemonInfo; test changed pid/port/startedAt/projectPath.
JetBrains tests pass under the jetbrains-gradle lease; coordinate MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt edits with the RF sequence.

implementationPlan.description:
SUPERVISOR READER: bounded, read-only, cross-OS. Load test-driven-development: write each test row, watch it fail for the expected reason, then implement.

Prerequisites. dependsOn gates the claim, not the bytes. Confirm that task-ec64165c (CQ-RF03) and task-90664db1 are DONE. Then read their landed MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt, MoeProjectService.kt, DaemonIdentity.kt and test files, and these memories:
- mem:task-task-ec64165c85f246088a7224cf70b04670-handoff

- mem:gotcha-jetbrains-read-daemon-info-deletes
- mem:gotcha-jetbrains-replacement-retry-guard

Where the landed names differ from this plan's, use the landed names. Never add a second parser, path normalizer or stop runner.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:
1. One bounded, read-only parse: private parseDaemonInfo(file: File): DaemonInfo?.
   - It is exactly today's read: readNBytes(MAX_DAEMON_JSON_BYTES + 1), today's 'larger than 64 KiB' warn, then gson.fromJson of the UTF-8 text.
   - It returns null when the file is absent, oversize, unreadable, malformed or JSON null. It never deletes and never throws.
   - replacementMetadataCleared (RF03) uses it instead of its own copy, with the same semantics: absent gives true; unparseable gives false; parsed gives pid > 0 && !isProcessAlive(pid). Fix its comment: readDaemonInfo no longer deletes, but its null still also means unreadable or another project.
2. The same-project rule, a companion `internal fun isSameProject(path: String, base: String): Boolean`.
   - First check DaemonIdentityProbe.comparableProjectPath(path) == comparableProjectPath(base). It is pure, with no IO, and covers the drive, forward-slash, case, trailing-separator, /mnt/<d>, //wsl$ and wsl.localhost spellings.
   - Only then check today's File(path).canonicalPath == File(base).canonicalPath, which covers symlinks, relative paths and 8.3 names.
   - Checking the comparable form first keeps a /mnt or //wsl$ spelling from ever reaching canonicalPath on Windows. Exceptions propagate to the caller.
3. readDaemonInfo() becomes read-only. It parses with (1).
   - An empty projectPath is accepted, as today.
   - The same project returns the info.
   - Another project logs a warn ('Ignoring .moe/daemon.json: it names <path>, not <base>') and returns null. Nothing is deleted.
   - Any exception logs at debug and returns null, as today. Gson leaves an absent projectPath null, and an invalid path throws.
4. `fun deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(expected: DaemonInfo): Boolean`.
   - Re-parse with (1). Delete only when the result == expected: data-class equality over port, pid, startedAt and projectPath.
   - It returns true only when this call removed the file.
   - A blank basePath returns false, so a relative .moe/daemon.json is never touched.
   - Error handling: it never throws. A failed delete is logged at warn and returns false.
5. ensureDaemonRunningImpl keeps today's self-heal, without readDaemonInfo's side effect.
   - Where today's cleanup sits (before the spawn-attempt and cooldown checks), remove the daemon.json it read through (4) when that file either:
     - names this project but is not reachable (today's branch), or
     - names another project (formerly readDaemonInfo's delete).
   - Keep a daemon.json that is absent or unparseable, or whose sameness check threw, as today.
   - Parse once and classify the file (this project / another project / unjudgeable) rather than parsing twice.

moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt. Build every alternative spelling from the exact string passed as basePath, and pass root.canonicalPath: Windows TEMP may hold 8.3 names.
- Replace `readDaemonInfo deletes a daemon file for another project` with `readDaemonInfo ignores but keeps a daemon file for another project`: two calls each return null, and the file stays byte-identical.
- `readDaemonInfo reads this project in every spelling`.
  - Drive base: as given, with forward slashes, lower-cased, with a trailing separator, and as /mnt/<d>/<rest>.
  - POSIX base: as given, with a trailing slash, with a /./ segment, as //wsl$/Ubuntu<path>, and in the backslash \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu share form.
  - For each spelling, write daemon.json with that projectPath. readDaemonInfo returns that port, pid, startedAt and projectPath, and the file stays byte-identical.
  - Per row, assert comparableProjectPath(spelling) == comparableProjectPath(base), so a broken fixture fails loudly.
  - A small private helper builds the other side's spelling, by the same rule as MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest's wslSpelling.
- An isSameProject literal table, the same on every host.
  - True: (/mnt/d/proj, D:\proj), (D:/proj/, D:\proj), (d:\PROJ, D:\proj), (D:\proj, /mnt/d/proj), (\\wsl$\Ubuntu\home\me\p, /home/me/p).
  - False: (D:\other, D:\proj), (/mnt/d/other, D:\proj).
  - No false row may use a UNC literal: on Windows its canonicalPath would touch the network.
- `ensureDaemonRunning removes another project's daemon file and spawns`, under LEGACY with a live pid and an open port: it returns true, processStarter is called once, and the file is gone.
- deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged:
  - an unchanged file is removed (true);
  - a file differing in exactly one of pid, port, startedAt or projectPath is kept byte for byte (false);
  - an oversize file is kept, and an absent one gives false.

No test starts or signals a real process: processStarter, processAliveProbe and portProbe are all injected.

implementationPlan.description:
SUPERVISOR: the other side of the Windows/WSL boundary.

A daemon.json written by a daemon on the other side carries a pid from another pid namespace (mem:gotcha-daemon-lifecycle-wsl-foreign). On a Windows IDE, a /mnt/<d> daemon.json comes from a WSL daemon whose pid Windows cannot see. Without this step, step 1 would hand that file to:
- the dead-pid branches, which delete it before the probe;
- LEGACY Restart Daemon, which would destroy whatever local process has that pid number.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:
1. A companion `internal fun isOtherSideOfWsl(projectPath: String, windows: Boolean): Boolean`. Port the two regexes of packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts isForeignDaemonInfo verbatim:
   - windows: the path starts with one slash that is not followed by a second slash or a backslash (an absolute POSIX path);
   - otherwise: a drive letter, a colon and a slash or backslash; or two slashes/backslashes followed by a non-slash (a drive or UNC path).
   Relative and empty paths are local. Call sites pass isWindows().
2. `fun isReachable(info: DaemonInfo): Boolean = (other side || isProcessAlive(info.pid)) && isPortOpen(info.port)`. An other-side daemon is judged by its port here, then by doConnect's /health probe.
3. ensureDaemonRunningImpl uses isReachable.
   - A reachable other-side info returns false BEFORE replacedUnverified. Nothing is spawned, and RF03 never looks up, captures, confirms or stops that pid. The installed CLI's stop refuses an other-side daemon.json anyway.
   - An unreachable one falls through to step 1's compare-delete cleanup and the spawn, as today. That covers the leftover file after wsl --shutdown.
4. stopDaemonForRestart(info) gets a new first line, before any pid check or lookup, in both profiles. An other-side info returns this fixed refusal:
   Restart Daemon did not stop pid <pid>, which .moe/daemon.json names on the other side of the Windows/WSL boundary: this IDE can neither see nor signal processes there. Check what that process is and stop it there yourself if it is a Moe daemon, then use Restart Daemon.
   - The text never calls that pid a Moe daemon.
   - Leave everything below that line byte-identical. CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a) rewrites it after this task and keeps this line first (comment-663bd16c on that row).

Tests in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisorTest.kt:
- isOtherSideOfWsl.
  - windows = true: /mnt/d/x and /home/u/x are true. //server/share/x, \\server\share, D:\x, D:/x, x, . and the empty string are false.
  - windows = false: //server/share/x, \\server\share, D:\x and D:/x are true. /mnt/d/x, /home/u/x, x, . and the empty string are false.
- isReachable.
  - Same side: a dead pid or a closed port each give false.
  - Other side: only the port counts. Record the pids processAliveProbe receives, and assert that the other-side pid never reaches it.
- `ensureDaemonRunning leaves an open other-side daemon of this project alone`, under LEGACY. projectPath is the other side's spelling of base, processAliveProbe = { false }, and the port is open.
  - Result: false, processStarter is never called, and the file stays byte-identical.
  - With the port closed: true (spawned), and the file is removed.
- PROTECTED, using RF03's ReplacementFixture. daemon.json is f.info.copy(projectPath = the other side's spelling of f.root.path), f.targetAlive = false, and the port is open. Expect ensureDaemonRunning() to return false, f.asked and f.commands to be empty, and the file to stay byte-identical.
- stopDaemonForRestart with an other-side info, under LEGACY and under PROTECTED.
  - processAliveProbe records its calls and returns true; processLookup returns a fake that counts destroy.
  - The result equals the refusal text exactly, with zero probe calls, zero lookups and zero destroys.
  - A same-side info under LEGACY still destroys once, as today.

Error handling: isReachable never throws, because isProcessAlive and isPortOpen already catch. The refusal path touches no process.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
The JetBrains plugin stops deleting or signaling on the strength of a path-string mismatch or a pid it cannot see.
(1) MoeDaemonSupervisor.readDaemonInfo is bounded and read-only. It returns daemon.json's info when projectPath names this project in any spelling (DaemonIdentityProbe.comparableProjectPath first, then canonicalPath). It returns null when the file is absent, oversize, malformed or names another project. It never deletes.
(2) A daemon.json written on the other side of the Windows/WSL boundary carries a pid from another pid namespace. That is an absolute POSIX projectPath read on Windows, or a drive or UNC one read elsewhere (the daemon's isForeignDaemonInfo). Its liveness is its port alone (isReachable). A reachable one is never spawned over, replaced by RF03 or signaled (Restart Daemon refuses with a fixed text), and doConnect's /health probe judges it.
(3) Every removal of daemon.json in MoeDaemonSupervisor and in MoeProjectService.connect()/handleForeignDaemon is a compare-delete (deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged). The file goes only while it still parses to the exact DaemonInfo (port, pid, startedAt, projectPath) the decision used.
(4) A daemon.json naming another project is still removed before this project's daemon is spawned, as today. ensureDaemonRunningImpl's compare-delete now does it, instead of readDaemonInfo.
acceptanceCriteria: readDaemonInfo returns null for another project's daemon.json on repeated calls, and the file stays byte-identical.

readDaemonInfo returns the info, leaving the file byte-identical, for these spellings of this project: drive, forward-slash, lower-case, trailing-separator and /mnt/<d> on a Windows host; trailing-slash, dot-segment, //wsl$ and wsl.localhost-share on a POSIX host.

ensureDaemonRunning with an other-side spelling of this project, whose pid is not alive here and whose port is open, returns false. It starts nothing, prompts nothing, runs no stop and keeps the file byte-identical, under both LEGACY and PROTECTED. Under LEGACY with the port closed, it removes the file and spawns.
ensureDaemonRunning removes another project's daemon.json and spawns, as today.
stopDaemonForRestart on an other-side info returns the fixed refusal, under both profiles. It never calls processAliveProbe or processLookup and destroys nothing.
handleForeignDaemon keeps, byte for byte, a daemon.json that changed in exactly one of pid, port, startedAt or projectPath since it was read. It still removes an unchanged one.
invariants: Outside two deletes that this task does not touch, the plugin removes .moe/daemon.json only by compare-delete against the DaemonInfo its decision used. The two are restartDaemon's post-stop delete (CQ-RF04's) and MoeMessageDispatcher's STATE_SNAPSHOT delete (task-007c0ea8).
No pid read from an other-side daemon.json reaches isProcessAlive, processLookup, destroy or RF03's replacement.
activationRefusal, verifyProvenance, the protected start/stop commands and RF03's same-side replacement flow are unchanged.
Every daemon.json read stays bounded by MAX_DAEMON_JSON_BYTES and never throws to its caller.
compatibility: Existing daemon.json files parse as before. Invalid JSON, JSON null, an oversize file or a missing projectPath still read as null, and the file is kept.
The public signatures of readDaemonInfo, getDaemonInfo, isProcessAlive, isPortOpen and stopDaemonForRestart are unchanged; new members are additive.
RF03's RP rows, RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest R1-R4 and task-90664db1's MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest rows pass unchanged.

sourceAssumptions: MoeDaemonSupervisor.readDaemonInfo compares File(info.projectPath).canonicalPath with File(base).canonicalPath and deletes daemon.json on a mismatch (HEAD 8f62fa0f, about lines 62-87).
ensureDaemonRunningImpl treats info as running only when isProcessAlive(pid) && isPortOpen(port). Otherwise it deletes daemon.json unconditionally before spawning (about lines 113-126).
MoeProjectService.connect() deletes daemon.json unconditionally when !isProcessAlive || !isPortOpen. connectWithRetry adopts the daemon when isProcessAlive && isPortOpen.

The daemon CLI's start removes a same-side daemon.json that names another project, but refuses an other-side one (exit 1, never removing it). Its stop sends no signal for an other-side daemon.json. See packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts existingDaemonBlocksStart and stopDaemon.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Swap only readDaemonInfo's path compare, the task's literal scope. Rejected. A /mnt/<d> daemon.json on a Windows IDE comes from a WSL daemon whose pid Windows cannot see. ensureDaemonRunningImpl's and connect()'s dead-pid branches would still delete it before the probe. Worse, once readDaemonInfo returns such infos, LEGACY Restart Daemon would destroy whatever local process has that pid number. That would be a new hazard, so step 2 is part of this task.
- Make readDaemonInfo read-only and stop there. Rejected: nothing would remove another project's daemon.json any more. The daemon CLI's start removes a same-side one itself, but it refuses an other-side one (exit 1, and it never removes it), so the IDE would wedge on a moved or copied project. Step 1.5 moves today's removal to spawn time, as a compare-delete.
- Judge other-side metadata by /health inside isReachable. Rejected: connect() can run on the EDT. doConnect already probes off the EDT, so a port check here plus that probe reaches the same verdict without a blocking HTTP call.
- For Restart Daemon on other-side metadata, return null, so restartDaemon deletes and spawns (today's outcome). Rejected in favour of a fixed refusal, like the daemon CLI's stop ('stop it from there'). Deleting and spawning puts two daemons on one .moe/ while the WSL daemon is alive.
